Get Off the Internet

Look up gun ranges in your area. Look for ones that have rentals and that offer classes. If you can find one that does both, jackpot!

Go visit. Let those real, physical people know that you want to learn more and (succinctly) why. You will be welcomed. Since you found a range with rentals and classes, you then rent some thing(s) like what you think you want to own, and start getting a feel for what guns like that are like.

When / if you want more hands-on help, take a class there - they'll get to know you and it'll be sweet.

Now Get On the Internet

While you're doing this, use the internet to further research things you hear about or see or experience during your trips to the range. Shot 2 new rifles? Look 'em up and find demo / teardown YouTube videos and see what people are saying about them. Look up the manufacturer and see what else they offer.

Most likely you'll want different guns to keep you "safe in the fields" than "wherever I go too". Build a relationship with the humans at your local range, and look online.

Now Buy a Gun

Now you have a lot of experience with guns that are appropriate for the kinds of things you want to use a gun for, and you have some experienced friends (at your local range) to consult if you're uncertain. Pick one and go buy it!

If you've done the above things and still aren't sure what to get - even after renting a bunch of different guns and trying them, here's a cheat sheet that you shouldn't take as gospel because that would indicate that you aren't actually ready to own a firearm, and also because I definitely am not an expert in all these areas.

I want to... So I need a... Like, for example...
Protect myself and my loved ones as we go about our daily lives Concealable handgun S&W MP 9
Protect my home from intruders Shotgun Mossberg 930 w/ Pistol Grip
Protect myself from (medium-sized) wild animals outdoors Ranch Rifle Henry "Big Boy" Steel .44 Magnum
Protect myself from government tyrrany Assault Rifle Ruger AR-556
Hunt Game Hunting Rifle No. Figure out what you want to hunt, then come back.
Hunt Birds Shotgun Mossberg 500 Hunting
Shoot moving targets for fun (e.g. skeet shooting) Shotgun (see above)
Enjoy target-shooting, cheaply .22 Rifle: Ruger 10/22 - Pistol: Walther PPK/S .22
Own a Piece of History Gun from WWI or WWII Mauser C96

Disclaimer #1

Of the above, I

  1. Own a S&W MP 9 and am pleased with it.
  2. Own a Henry .22 rifle, and love it.

The rest is an (sometimes un-)educated guess.

But really, Henry rifles are beautiful works of art.

Disclaimer #2

Guns are usually not single-purpose tools. You can totally skeet shoot with a home-defense shotgun, you can take any of them to the range to shoot targets, you can protect your home with your concealed-carry handgun, and you can do almost all of these thigns with AR-15s... for example.

Mostly I like making tables.

Disclaimer #3

Accept that you may not like a gun that you purchase. Maybe it's finicky, maybe it's uncomfortable, maybe you just think it's ugly. Guns are pretty good at retaining their resale value. Sell it (check local and state and federal laws!) or trade it if you don't like it. Eventually, you'll find one you do.
